claims.text: Introducing a coherent L12 phase into HEAs can improve resistance to thermally induced toughness loss.
The target HEAs are initially single-phase.
A coherent L12 phase can act as a strengthener in HEAs.
HEAs tend to decompose into multiple phases above 500 °C.
The coherent L12 phase may enhance resistance to thermally induced degradation through strengthening.
The L12 phase may reduce the mobility of interstitials and vacancies.
Reduced interstitial and vacancy mobility suppresses radiation-induced segregation.
Suppressing radiation-induced segregation enhances the alloy's thermal stability.
HEA tensile strength can degrade severely at elevated temperatures.
Introducing coherent L12 should enhance elevated-temperature mechanical properties.
HEAs without coherent L12 may have lower thermal stability than otherwise comparable L12-strengthened HEAs.
HEAs without coherent L12 may undergo greater elevated-temperature toughness loss.
The effectiveness of L12 strengthening may depend on alloy composition.
The effectiveness of L12 strengthening may depend on the L12 phase fraction.
The effectiveness of L12 strengthening may depend on temperature and the solvus of the strengthening phase.
The exact mechanism by which L12 enhances thermal stability is not fully understood.
A controlled comparison of otherwise comparable HEAs with and without coherent L12 at elevated temperature can test the hypothesis.
Failure of the L12-containing HEA to improve thermal stability and mechanical properties relative to the control would falsify the proposed benefit.

contradictions.description: The stated domain is specifically above 500 °C, but the proposed example experiment is at 500 °C, which is not above that boundary.

The hypothesis concerns thermally induced toughness loss, whereas the proposed mechanism centers on radiation-induced segregation without specifying irradiation as a condition or connecting that process directly to toughness.
The central outcome is toughness retention, but the falsification rule refers broadly to thermal stability and mechanical properties and does not require a decisive toughness measurement.
